newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain insurers study ways to face competition.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain insurers study ways to face competition.

text.p: Bahrain insurance companies are studying ways to improve service and face competition from international and other Gulf insurers, a newspaper said on Wednesday.
Gulf Daily News said the Bahrain Insurance Association (BIA) and five insurance firms would finance a 42,000 dinar ($111,400) study to evaluate the insurance market in the Gulf Arab state.
"The study is aimed at helping us prepare ourselves for the impending competition we face from GCC and international companies," it quoted BIA deputy chairman Hameed al-Nasser as saying.
"At present, we are competing among ourselves but the question is whether we are capable of competing with GCC companies and with international players," Nasser said.
The GCC, a political and economic alliance, groups Bahrain, Oman, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
Nasser said the study would examine options available to Bahrain insurance firms including "mergers and capital injections".
Nasser said insurance rates in Bahrain were often higher than in other GCC states "because the volumes in other GCC states were much greater than in Bahrain".

"BIA members are concerned that regional insurers will find it attractive to enter the Bahrain market, with lower rates. We need to protect ourselves from companies...which will be in a position to dominate the market," Nasser said.
